title: Shift coherence of a derived square computed on K-injectives
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal A',\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_{\mathcal E}:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal E)\to D(\mathcal E)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$ be additive functors, and let $t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ and $r:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$ be exact additive functors, with a specified natural isomorphism $\delta:rF\xrightarrow{\sim}Gt$. Write $C(H)$ for termwise application of a functor $H$, and $r_D,t_D$ for the exact derived functors, with their canonical factorization isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. A complex $I$ is K-injective if every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. Assume every complex in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$ admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex, and $C(t)$ preserves K-injective complexes. Fix right-derived presentations $RF,RG$, with natural comparison maps $\eta^F_K:Q_{\mathcal B}C(F)K\to RF(Q_{\mathcal A}K)$ and $\eta^G_J:Q_{\mathcal B'}C(G)J\to RG(Q_{\mathcal A'}J)$ that are isomorphisms on K-injectives. Give $RF,RG$ the shifts computed using $I[n]$ for a K-injective representative $I$, and give $r_D,t_D$ the termwise shifts. Let $\gamma:r_D RF\xrightarrow{\sim}RG t_D$ be a natural isomorphism normalized on every complex $K$ by
$$\gamma_{Q_{\mathcal A}K}\circ r_D(\eta^F_K)=\eta^G_{C(t)K}\circ Q_{\mathcal B'}(C(\delta)_K),$$
where the exact factorization isomorphisms for $r,t$ are inserted on both sides. Then, under the computation isomorphisms for any K-injective representative $I$ of $E\in D(\mathcal A)$, $\gamma_E$ is represented by $C(\delta)_I:C(r)C(F)I\to C(G)C(t)I$. For every integer $n$,
$$s_{RGt_D,n,E}\circ\gamma_{E[n]}=\gamma_E[n]\circ s_{r_DRF,n,E},$$
where $s$ denotes the composite shift comparisons. On the shifted K-injective model, both routes are represented in degree $a$ by $\delta_{I^{a+n}}$ and have the signed differential $(-1)^n d$. These assertions concern the specified normalized comparison, not an independently chosen derived isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open, proof using a K-injective representative and its restriction; preceding exact-restriction discussion and Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open. Abstract additive-square and integer-shift refinement by the agent.

proof.text: Write $A=r_DRF$ and $B=RGt_D$. For an exact functor $h$, write $\varphi^h_L:h_DQ(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}QC(h)L$ for its factorization. Fix a K-injective $I$ and set $a_I=r_D(\eta^F_I)\circ(\varphi^r_{C(F)I})^{-1}:QC(r)C(F)I\to A(QI)$ and $b_I=RG((\varphi^t_I)^{-1})\circ\eta^G_{C(t)I}:QC(G)C(t)I\to B(QI)$. The cited factorization theorem supplies both $\varphi$ isomorphisms. The hypothesis on $C(t)$ makes $C(t)I$ K-injective, so both comparison maps $\eta$ here are isomorphisms by the assumptions of the item; hence $a_I,b_I$ are isomorphisms. These are precisely the computation isomorphisms, with their directions fixed.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; abstract notation for the computation in sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open

proof.text: Apply the assumed normalization at $K=I$, inserting the factorization maps with the directions in Step 1. It says exactly $\gamma_{QI}\circ a_I=b_I\circ Q(C(\delta)_I)$. Multiplication by $a_I^{-1}$ gives $\gamma_{QI}=b_I\circ Q(C(\delta)_I)\circ a_I^{-1}$. If $e:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ is any specified representative isomorphism, set $a_{I,e}=A(e)\circ a_I$ and $b_{I,e}=B(e)\circ b_I$. Naturality gives $\gamma_E\circ A(e)=B(e)\circ\gamma_{QI}$, hence $\gamma_E\circ a_{I,e}=b_{I,e}\circ Q(C(\delta)_I)$. This proves the first assertion for every representative, without a new choice of derived isomorphism.

source.place: Agent refinement of sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0D6G: apply the specified normalization and naturality

proof.text: Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$. The cited shift lemma makes $I[n]$ K-injective, and makes the shift of a K-injective resolution a resolution of the shifted complex. Since $C(t)$ preserves K-injectives, $C(t)(I[n])$ is also K-injective. For any additive $H$, the identity in degree $a$ identifies $C(H)(I[n])$ with $(C(H)I)[n]$: both have $H(I^{a+n})$ and differential $H((-1)^nd)=(-1)^nH(d)$. Thus the stipulated computation of all four functors at $E[n]$ uses the same shifted model, including when $n$ is negative.

source.place: Tag 070H, definition-K-injective and its following remark; signed shift convention and termwise additivity

proof.text: Put $u_I=C(\delta)_I$ and use the identity termwise shift identifications of Step 3. In degree $a$, both $u_{I[n]}$ and $u_I[n]$ are $\delta_{I^{a+n}}$. They are chain maps: naturality of $\delta$ for $d:I^{a+n}\to I^{a+n+1}$ says $Gt(d)\circ\delta_{I^{a+n}}=\delta_{I^{a+n+1}}\circ rF(d)$; multiplying this equality by $(-1)^n$ gives the chain-map equation for the shifted differentials. Hence $u_{I[n]}=u_I[n]$, with no extra sign on the component of $\delta$. This is a direct calculation from additivity and naturality, not an additional comparison theorem.

source.place: Agent integer-shift refinement of Tag 0D6G; cochain shift convention in derived.tex

proof.text:
First take $E=QI$ and insert the localization shift isomorphisms $Q(L[n])\cong Q(L)[n]$. By the stipulated shifts of $RF,RG$ computed on shifted K-injectives, their computation isomorphisms intertwine these shifts. Clause (2) of the cited exact factorization theorem says the same for $\varphi^r,\varphi^t$. Composing these equalities in the definitions of $a_I,b_I$ in Step 1 yields $s_{A,n,QI}\circ a_{I[n]}=a_I[n]$ and $s_{B,n,QI}\circ b_{I[n]}=b_I[n]$, where $Q(I[n])$ is identified with $(QI)[n]$. Consequently
$$s_{B,n,QI}\circ\gamma_{(QI)[n]}\circ a_{I[n]}=b_I[n]\circ Q(u_{I[n]})=b_I[n]\circ Q(u_I)[n]=\gamma_{QI}[n]\circ a_I[n]=\gamma_{QI}[n]\circ s_{A,n,QI}\circ a_{I[n]}.$$
The first and third equalities are Step 2 at $I[n]$ and $I$, respectively; the middle equality is Step 4 and shift compatibility of $Q$. Cancel the isomorphism $a_{I[n]}$. This proves the required shift equation at $QI$ and shows both routes have the component and signed differential computed in Step 4.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor and the termwise shift compatibility; agent normalization calculation refining Tag 0D6G

proof.text: Every $E\in D(\mathcal A)$ has such a representative: $Q$ is a localization of $\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $E\cong QK$ for a complex $K$; by hypothesis there is a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective, and $Q$ inverts it, giving $e:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}E$. For a general $e:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}E$, naturality of $\gamma$ and of both composite shift comparisons gives $s_{B,n,E}\circ\gamma_{E[n]}\circ A(e[n])=B(e)[n]\circ s_{B,n,QI}\circ\gamma_{(QI)[n]}$ and $\gamma_E[n]\circ s_{A,n,E}\circ A(e[n])=B(e)[n]\circ\gamma_{QI}[n]\circ s_{A,n,QI}$. The right sides agree by Step 5, and $A(e[n])$ is an isomorphism, so cancellation gives the desired equation at $E$. Step 2 fixes $\gamma_E$ under every computation isomorphism; no claim about an independently chosen natural isomorphism is needed.
